neighbours.label: Auxiliary or copula opening a 'what'/'that' clause about an earlier or later stage, just before a time adverb (what was once, that would later, what critics have long); promotes later, eventually, once
fire: The settlers built a fort on land that would later become the state capital.
Our guesthouse occupies what was once a busy textile mill by the canal.
Engineers have finally proven what critics have long argued about the dam.
The firm began in a garage, in what would eventually be known as Silicon Valley.
This café stands in what was formerly the town's main post office.
A young clerk drafted the plan that would ultimately reshape the railway.
Historians have now documented what villagers have always said about the famine.
The trail follows what had originally been a Roman road through the hills.
quiet: The settlers built a fort on land near the state capital.
Our guesthouse occupies a busy textile mill by the canal.
Engineers have finally inspected the cracks along the old dam.
The firm began in a garage near Palo Alto in a rented house.
This café stands beside the town's main post office on the square.
A young clerk drafted a plan to reshape the railway.
Historians have documented the famine in several villages.
The trail follows a Roman road through the hills.

short: aux before time adverb in clause
